To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

All-optical clocked SR, D, JK, and T flip-flops have been proposed and demonstrated, exploiting SOA-based SR latches and optical logic gates, with operation speed limited by the SOAs bandwidth, and that photonic integration is a viable approach to increase the speed beyond GHz.
all-optical clocking of flip-flops can be achieved using logic gates based on FWM and XGM nonlinearities, which are integrated in the SOA-based SR latch.

All-optical clocked SR flip-flops are obtained by combining a SOA-based gain quenching bi-stable element and optical logic gates, exploiting four wave mixing and cross gain modulation nonlinear effects in SOAs.

the design and demonstration of all-optical flip-flop schemes that can be easily implemented in future photonic integrated circuits.

a wide variety of all-optical flip-flop functionalities, including clocked operation, can be realized by employing only two basic building blocks, a bi-stable element (SOA based SR latch) and logic gates (FWM and XGM).
the proposed flip-flops are based on simple and robust schemes, which can be readily integrated on a single chip.
